change.title: pr-7
change.description: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes
change.author: Jeff Atwood

findings.title: Light-theme value for reply-history usernames swapped from 30% to 70%
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light-theme argument is 70% and the dark-theme argument is `$secondary` 30%. The arguments are inverted compared with every other conversion in this PR, which maps N% on `$primary` to (100−N)% on `$secondary`. `dark-light-choose` returns the first argument when `$primary` is darker (common/foundation/variables.scss:46-51), so on the default light theme the bold `.topic-meta-data h5 a` link becomes much paler. On dark themes it renders dim instead of light. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme value for .custom-message-length changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new code passes 30% for the light theme and `$secondary` 70% for the dark theme, which is the reverse of the PR's mapping. The desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss:94) uses 70%/30%. On light themes this hint text becomes much darker, and on dark themes it becomes bright rather than muted. Swap it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50% on light themes
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new light-theme argument is 50%, so the light theme also changes, not only the dark one, and the PR description says nothing about that. The desktop equivalent (desktop/topic-post.scss:321) keeps 20%/80%. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: Group member .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% on light themes
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code uses 50%/50%, which makes the member name the same colour as `.title` directly below it (line 527). That removes the visual difference between name and title on the light theme. Keep 30% and use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. mobile/user.scss:497 has the same change.

findings.title: Group member .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% on light themes (mobile)
findings.body: This is the same regression as desktop/user.scss:522. The old value was 30% on `$primary` and the new one is 50%/50%, so the name now matches `.title` (line 503). Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

summary: The PR wraps `scale-color($primary, N%)` calls in `dark-light-choose(…, scale-color($secondary, (100−N)%))` so dark themes get matching values. The helper returns the first argument on light themes (common/foundation/variables.scss:46-51), so most conversions leave light themes unchanged. Five of them are not mechanical and change the light-theme colour. desktop/topic-post.scss:291 and mobile/modal.scss:102 have the two arguments inverted. mobile/topic-post.scss:182 and both user.scss group-member `.name` rules change the light-theme lightness value. embed.css.scss imports variables, so the helper is available there.
